SMTO-MON-0011 — A continuous monitor needs a stop time

GUID: c6725c5b-a855-4ab5-9fd4-e68736bc6fd0
Slug: monitor-stream-unbounded
Domain: MON · Subsystem: mon

What happened

  • This monitor follows a command's output continuously (like watch or tail -f), but no time limit was set, so SMTO didn't start it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the agent to start the monitor again with a time limit, for example “watch it for 10 minutes”. Continuous monitors must stop on their own, so SMTO needs to know how long to run.
  2. If you don't need live output, ask for a monitor that checks at regular times instead, such as every 30 seconds. A regular check runs the command and finishes each time, so it doesn't need a continuous stream.

What success looks like

  • The monitor starts, and its summary shows how long it will run.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the request without a time limit; it will be rejected the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • monitor_command_rejection_reason rejected a raw_stream monitor because duration_seconds is missing or not positive.

What this means

  • A raw_stream command reaches validation without a positive duration_seconds value. Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.

Why this can happen

  • A raw_stream command reaches validation without a positive duration_seconds value.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect raw_stream mode and its effective duration independently of sample-command scheduling.

How to fix it

  • Set a positive duration_seconds before starting a raw_stream monitor (watch or tail -f commands); drafted durations are clamped to max_inferred_monitor_duration_seconds. The check is monitor_command_rejection_reason in src/agent_runtime/monitors/drafting.py.
  • Set a positive bounded monitoring duration before starting the stream.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A positive supported bounded duration is present before stream admission.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
